## Abstract

Most human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are cutaneous beta- and gamma-types residing on skin as commensals, yet their role in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is contested between "hit-and-run" oncogenic and protective-immunity models. Because standard pipelines discard the non-human reads carrying HPV signal, we re-mined public human RNA-seq across skin with a pipeline that screens each library for papillomavirus reads, types positives against the full panel, and scores productive infection from late (L1 major-capsid) transcripts. To control the two confounders, we flagged cell-line and engineered material and scored each library as papillomavirus reads-per-million. HPV signal was concentrated in non-primary material: cell-line and engineered libraries were five-fold enriched for positivity (OR `r fo(min(stats$cl_or, stats$eng_or))`–`r fo(max(stats$cl_or, stats$eng_or))`, *P* < 10⁻⁸), dominated by integrated HPV16/HPV18, whereas primary skin carried HPV at only 2–4%. Productive infection was abundant in warts and epidermodysplasia verruciformis (`r round(stats$m3_ctrl_pct)`% of libraries). By contrast, cSCC and actinic keratosis, though sequenced four times more deeply, reached the detection floor in only `r pp(stats$neo_pctfloor)`% of libraries versus `r pp(stats$ctrl_pctfloor)`% of controls (Fisher OR `r fo(stats$fish_or)`), with median burden six orders of magnitude lower. Depth-adjusted, neoplasia sat marginally above unselected skin (OR `r fo(stats$m2b_or)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2b_p)`), but only as a trace footprint (any-read OR `r fo(stats$m2a_or)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2a_p)`) that deeper sequencing never made productive. A minority of lesions harboured genuine productive gamma-/alpha-HPV infection (HPV12, HPV96, HPV182, HPV16). Cutaneous HPV is productive in warts but quiet in healthy skin and carcinoma: a trace, non-productive footprint both models must accommodate. Beyond HPV, this contamination-aware, depth-normalised framework can mine the discarded fraction of public transcriptomes.

**Keywords:** human papillomavirus; beta-papillomavirus; cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; skin virome; productive infection; hit-and-run; RNA-seq; public data re-mining; contamination
